races.name: Racing To School Reaches 250,000 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with strong recent course-level form (two wins from last three), handles good ground well (11/15 positive sim-going record), and benefits enormously from an uncontested lead under Sam Twiston-Davies; the STYLE_FIT tag signals he is operating in a slightly forward role relative to his natural P habit, but at this trip and field size the distinction is negligible.

runners_data.name: Manyana Blue
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose form string of 21222 screams consistent placing rather than winning, and the 257-day absence is the single biggest risk factor; Luke Scott (3) is an apprentice-level conditional and the horse's best going figures are split between soft and good, making the good-to-firm surface something to monitor, though the prominent style maps cleanly onto the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies whose recent form (9-3432) shows a step back from the placed level, and the H style is the least advantaged profile given the modest pace a lone front-runner in a three-horse field will generate; James Turner (5) is an inexperienced conditional, and the OR of 86 leaves her conceding weight at the top of the handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Gore Point is the lone front-runner here and, with only two rivals to contend with, will bowl along at the head of affairs from the outset without any meaningful pressure applied by the prominent-tracking Manyana Blue. Miss Denver is a hold-up type who will settle at the rear and look to close late, but with just three runners over 2m½f on good-to-firm ground, the field will not string out dramatically and fractions are unlikely to be truly searching. Gore Point's unchallenged lead at a sustainable clip means this race will be run to suit those who can travel comfortably in touch and pounce off the final bend rather than those who need a true test to reel in the leader. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track the tempo without expending energy, then produce a clean jump at the last — making the hold-up profile of Miss Denver the most disadvantaged by the expected dynamics.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Gore Point dictates a comfortable gallop and puts the race to bed from the front without being seriously pressed.
scenarios.body: Gore Point sets an uncontested, measured pace throughout and jumps economically under Sam Twiston-Davies, arriving at the last with enough in reserve to hold on; the small field and good-to-firm ground play directly to this tactic, as no rival can build the momentum to overhaul a horse in command.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Gore Point's stamina or jumping wavers in the closing stages and Manyana Blue can deliver a timely challenge off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Manyana Blue, tracking just off the pace throughout, pounces when the front-runner idles or makes a jumping error late; the 4yo's consistent placed form on good and good-to-firm ground makes this a credible secondary scenario despite the long absence of 257 days.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for Miss Denver off the final turn.
scenarios.body: Miss Denver sweeps past rivals in the straight having conserved energy from the back, but this relies on a pace scenario that a single front-runner in a three-horse field is unlikely to generate; the OR gap of 23lb from Gore Point and 15lb from Manyana Blue makes this a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Decide It
scenarios.trigger: If fencing errors from the leader disrupt the race order and hand an unexpected advantage to whichever rival is in the best position at the time.
scenarios.body: A costly mistake by Gore Point at a critical fence scrambles the expected shape and throws the contest open; with so few runners, any error is magnified, though the small field reduces collision risk and well-schooled horses tend to jump cleanly on sound ground.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gore Point's jumping closely — any error at a fence on the final circuit with only two rivals present could immediately hand Manyana Blue a decisive advantage that cannot be clawed back.
Manyana Blue's 257-day absence is the clearest red flag in the race; monitor paddock behaviour and early jumping fluency for signs the long layoff has left the four-year-old short of race fitness.

Miss Denver's hold-up style is structurally compromised in a three-runner race with no genuine pace pressure; if she gets too far detached from the small group early, James Turner (5) may lack the experience to correct the position tactically mid-race.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 2m½f trip — monitor any late going updates, as a further drying of the surface would compress finishing times and further entrench the front-runner's advantage.

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
Racing Club Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Renoir
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and likely to have things his own way from the outset; Good ground form is solid (sim-going 10/15, 1W4P) and the 47-day break is not a concern given Ben Clarke's 1/8 T14 strike rate; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects he is mapped as Prominent rather than true Lead but in this field he gets the lead by default, which is a positive rather than a negative.

runners_data.name: Get The Value
runners_data.note: John O'Shea's yard is firing (T14: 2/3) and Kielan Woods takes the ride on a horse with strong Good-ground credentials (11/15 sim-going, 2W4P); genuine hold-up type who needs a genuinely run race over this 18-22f range, and the steady pace is his main tactical risk.

runners_data.name: Sam's Amour
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose best form comes at 22-26f, suggesting this 18f trip is on the sharp side; Good ground suits (12/15 sim-going, 2W4P) and Tom Bellamy is a positive booking, but a steady pace at a shorter trip makes his finishing kick harder to deploy.

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who will look to sit just off Renoir and could be the horse who applies the first serious pressure; tongue-tie fitted, Joe Tizzard yard at 0/1 T14, and recent hurdles form reads 647-74 — needs to find improvement but the prominent position suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Privilege
runners_data.note: Consistent placed efforts on Good ground (2W2P, 12/15 sim-going) for the John & Rhys Flint yard, though T14 reads 0/7 which tempers confidence; likely to sit handy and is the natural type to be involved at the business end if Renoir weakens, but has not won for some time.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort (2nd, 18f, Good) most recently and has a consistent recent string of 4-P-3-4-2; Nick Scholfield as trainer is a new role for a former jockey and T14 reads 1/13 — not a hot yard, but this horse's form and racing style (genuine hold-up) give him a quiet each-way profile if the pace lifts.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Won last time (18f, Good) and handles this ground well (13/15 sim-going); true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map because of overcrowding at the rear — his natural finishing run will be compromised by the number of similar types around him, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) reflects that positional challenge rather than his absolute ability.

runners_data.name: Coup De Gold
runners_data.note: Most recent win was over 17f on Good, so the trip and ground are fine, but this 10-year-old is a genuine closer whose mapped midfield position understates the congestion he will face; amateur rider (7lb claim from Miss Eleanor Williams) is a notable factor, and the T14 of 0/5 does not inspire stable confidence.

runners_data.name: Hawa Jumeirah
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a limited hurdles record (form: 05-583) and a modest OR of 80; true hold-up runner placed into midfield by redistribution — the horse hasn't shown the consistent class to win from a compromised position, and the Helen Nelmes yard has 0/0 T14.

runners_data.name: Bowling Shane
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hurdler on an upward trajectory (latest: 3rd, 5th) but only 3/9 sim-going runs on this surface and the Ned Fox 3lb claim is the main positive; best form has come at 16-20f and the step to 18f is manageable, though form figures of 800-35 reflect inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Peace Motivator
runners_data.note: Recent form reads FP-PP8 which is deeply uninspiring; Barry John Murphy's yard is active (T14: 3/12) but this horse has a cluttered profile of falls, pulled-ups and distant finishes — true hold-up type mapped to midfield, meaning he'll face traffic issues on top of indifferent form.

runners_data.name: Anothermanicmonday
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 72) with a form string of 0P06-5 and only 3/6 sim-going runs; 60 days off the track and the Sue Gardner yard is at 1/4 T14 — natural hold-up horse repositioned into midfield due to the weight of closers in this field, adding positional difficulty to an already challenging profile.

races.paceDynamic: Renoir is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, he should be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 2m2½f at Newton Abbot. Ugo Bingo and Privilege are mapped as prominent but are unlikely to impose serious pressure on Renoir early, meaning this race will almost certainly be run at a steady-to-moderate tempo with a single leader controlling the fractions from the front. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Saucats, Coup De Gold, Hawa Jumeirah, Peace Motivator and Anothermanicmonday have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more genuine closers than the pace picture can accommodate at the rear, meaning those horses will be crowding for ground in the second half of the field without getting a clean solo stalking position. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a deliberate tempo — strongly favours horses racing prominently or able to travel fluently just off the pace, with closers carrying a structural disadvantage unless the winning rider asks an early question that strings the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Renoir Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Renoir leads unchallenged and the early gallop is steady enough that he retains reserves into the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Renoir dictates an uncontested pace and the lack of pressure means he never expends excess energy, allowing him to quicken away from the last on the Good to Firm ground he handles well; his sim-going record of 10/15 and prior placed efforts at this trip make him the natural beneficiary of a race run to suit a front-runner. Prominent horses who can sit just behind and travel into position — Ugo Bingo and Privilege — are best placed to mount any challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Apply Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Ugo Bingo or Privilege push forward early and apply enough pressure on Renoir to lift the tempo into a genuinely searching gallop.
scenarios.body: A more genuine pace tests Renoir's stamina and opens up the race for hold-up horses with strong finishes, but it also rewards those who can travel prominently and quicken off an honest gallop rather than a crawl; Get The Value's consistent sim-going form (11/15) and Sam's Amour's proven staying ability over 22f+ make them dangers under this shape. Raffles Nobu, who has shown placed efforts over similar ground, is also interesting if the pace lifts his finishing effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp A Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just deceptive enough to string the field out and Renoir weakens dramatically from the second-last, allowing the chasing pack to overwhelm him.
scenarios.body: Sam's Amour and Get The Value, genuine hold-up operators with strong Good ground records, are the natural winners of this shape — but this scenario is constrained by the number of redistributed hold-up types who will be fighting for the same ground rather than producing clean finishing runs. Saucats won last time out over 18f on Good ground and carries viable form, though his true style is buried in a crowded rear group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of hold-up types causes traffic problems late and an unconsidered runner from lower in the weights delivers a clean run at the right moment.
scenarios.body: Coup De Gold won most recently and Saucats has winning form on this ground, but both must race out of their natural positions due to field congestion, making a clean passage far from guaranteed; the beneficiary of any late scramble is more likely to be a horse like Bowling Shane, who has form at shorter trips and could find extra room in a compressed finish. This scenario requires a degree of misfortune for the principals and is the least structurally likely given the clean lead Renoir is expected to enjoy.

watchPoints.text: Renoir's true starting position will be critical — if he is slow away or Ugo Bingo bowls to the front instead, the entire pace map collapses and hold-up horses immediately become more dangerous.

The cluster of redistributed closers (Saucats, Coup De Gold, Hawa Jumeirah, Peace Motivator, Anothermanicmonday) will all be looking for room in the same part of the track from the home turn — watch for potential interference and horses checking or being hampered on the bend.

Get The Value is 13 days since last run for a trainer in form (T14: 2/3) — if the yard has specifically targeted this race, he could produce a peak effort that the steady pace does not fully suppress.

Coup De Gold's amateur rider (Miss Eleanor Williams, 7lb claim) is worth monitoring — the weight relief is meaningful in a handicap at this level but the positional compromise from redistribution may negate the claim advantage.

Sam's Amour's trip preference is 22-26f judged on his historical form; at 18f on a flat Newton Abbot circuit, watch whether Tom Bellamy elects to produce him very late to compensate, which could leave too much ground to make up against a leader in control.

races.name: Par Inn Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ellerton
runners_data.note: Won twice over similar Good ground and has strong course suitability at 2W5P on similar conditions; the one concern is the [STYLE_FIT] tag suggesting it may not be entirely at home dictating here, though as the lone confirmed pace-setter it will likely lead regardless — headgear (blinkers) may sharpen focus but 47 days off adds a fitness question.|

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Remarkable consistency with five consecutive placed efforts including four seconds, all on Good or similar ground, making it the most reliably performing horse in the field; races prominently and should sit a comfortable second, ready to challenge late — trainer Nick Scholfield has a poor 14-day strike rate (0/13) but the form profile speaks for itself.|

runners_data.name: The Gypsy Davey
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse that needs a strong pace to make ground from the rear, which this race is unlikely to generate; visor headgear is worn and the trainer has a modest 14-day record (1/8), while the recent form — four and four — suggests solid enough jumping but no real surge of form to suggest a step forward is coming.|

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls sends this seven-year-old out from 40 days off, but recent form includes a fall and a pulled-up which injects doubt about jumping reliability; a natural hold-up type at 91 OR who requires generous fractions, and with the race expected to run at a controlled tempo, getting competitive is a significant ask — hood headgear noted.|

races.paceDynamic: Ellerton is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and will set off to lead from the outset, with Limerick Leader also rated prominent — meaning those two will race close to or at the head of affairs over 2m5f on Good to Firm ground at Newton Abbot. With no genuine pace rival to push Ellerton hard, the gallop is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than searching, robbing the two hold-up horses — The Gypsy Davey and It's A Breeze — of the strong fractions they need to close from the rear. The tight four-runner field and honest but uncontested tempo point squarely toward a race that rewards horses who travel prominently and can jump efficiently, negating the hold-up profiles unless Ellerton or Limerick Leader make enough errors to bring the race back to the closers. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can dictate terms and see out the trip on quick ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ellerton Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Ellerton leads uncontested and sets a steady, controlled gallop that suits prominent types throughout.
scenarios.body: Ellerton bowls along in front with Limerick Leader tracking closely, and the lack of genuine pace pressure means the hold-up horses never get enough momentum to close meaningfully on the run-in. Prominent racers who jump fluently and stay the trip are directly rewarded in this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Limerick Leader Wears Ellerton Down
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader presses Ellerton persistently enough to drain his stamina and takes over at a late fence.
scenarios.body: Limerick Leader's consistent placed form at similar trips and going — with five consecutive top-three finishes including four runner-up slots — suggests it has the engine to collar a front-runner who has done too much work early. If Ellerton's jumping costs him momentum at a critical point, Limerick Leader is ideally placed to pounce and see out the longer 2m5f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected or jumping errors disrupt the leaders, creating enough of a gap for a closer to reel them in.
scenarios.body: The Gypsy Davey, the more active of the two hold-up types with stronger going form (14/15 similar-ground runs placed), would be best placed to benefit if the leaders tire on the climb to the finish. It's A Breeze has the Paul Nicholls stable angle but patchy recent form with a pulled-up and a fall in the string makes confidence fragile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jumping errors or a loose horse disrupts the race order and turns it into a scramble.
scenarios.body: In a field of only four with at least one horse carrying a fall in recent form (It's A Breeze — F in form string), a significant jumping incident could eliminate a fancied runner and hand an unlikely result to whoever survives cleanly. This scenario is inherently unpredictable but the tiny field means a single error carries outsized consequences.

watchPoints.text: Ellerton's jumping reliability under a controlled solo lead needs monitoring — any serious error mid-race at Newton Abbot's tricky fences could undo its natural tactical advantage immediately.
It's A Breeze has a fall in its recent form string; in a field of only four, any repeat jumping incident could materially alter the result and is worth tracking at the first few fences.
Limerick Leader's jockey James Bowen must judge how hard to press Ellerton — push too early and he could flatter to deceive, but leave it too late on a short run-in and the window closes fast.

The Gypsy Davey's visor is retained from recent runs but its hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged by the projected pace; watch whether Conor Ring attempts to ride more prominently than the horse's typical map suggests.

Going is officially Good to Firm for this race despite the card listing Good — the faster surface suits Ellerton and Limerick Leader's proven records on quick ground and may stretch the stamina of It's A Breeze over 2m5f.

races.name: William Hill Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Donald McCain, best recent form at 20-26f on Good, and sim-going record of 14/15 runners beaten suggests modest ability in this grade; 12 years old raises obvious stamina-versus-recovery questions over 3m2f, and Theo Gillard's claim may be the lure here.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton combine with a horse in good form (three placings from last four starts including a recent win), but the fade-in-finish flag is a significant concern at 3m2f; tongue-tie applied and sim-going record of 9/15 beaten hints he is workable but not dominant on this type of surface.

runners_data.name: Belgarum
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for Joe Tizzard — the style-fit tag (0.92) reflects that he is racing in his natural prominent role but the concern is sustaining it alone over an extended 3m2f trip; tongue-tie applied and his recent form includes a win and second from last three completed starts, making him the key pace reference throughout.

runners_data.name: Balkardy
runners_data.note: Mrs C Williams' nine-year-old arrives on a grim form string of P-U7P and has failed to finish in three of his last five starts; a genuine hold-up type shifted toward midfield in the race map, his nil wins and placings on similar going (6/15 assessed) make him the most obvious weak link, and the amateur rider adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's consistent eight-year-old has placed in four of his last five starts and boasts the strongest sim-going record in the field at 9/11 runners behind him; running from a prominent position on a track and ground combination that suits his profile, he is the most reliable each-way profile if Belgarum's lead is run down.

races.paceDynamic: Belgarum is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and should lead from the outset over 3m2f at Newton Abbot on Good to Firm ground, setting a sustainable and largely uncontested gallop. With no other natural pace-setter to challenge him, Belgarum can control tempo from flag to finish, which typically compresses the race and makes it difficult for hold-up horses to generate a meaningful winning surge late on. Balkardy is a genuine hold-up type but has been mapped to midfield given the field's profile — the redistribution note confirms the rear is crowded with similar types, meaning true hold-up horses like Presentandcounting and Muskerry Rock may struggle to find the daylight they need to deliver their finishing efforts. This race shape most strongly favours prominent or handy-tracking types who can travel close to Belgarum's controlled pace and produce a measured, sustained effort through the final stages rather than a sharp late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belgarum Controls, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Belgarum leads uncontested and sets a genuine but manageable gallop throughout the 3m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Belgarum dictates every yard at a rhythm that suits his stamina, and the lack of pressure means he arrives at the final fences with reserves intact; a prominent tracker who travels fluently close to him is ideally placed to capitalise if he tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Belgarum's solo lead produces a falsely slow early tempo and a horse tracking in second or third delivers a decisive run from the final fence.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn gallop stretches out over the long Newton Abbot circuit before quickening sharply late, catching Belgarum flat-footed at the finish; Muskerry Rock or Presentandcounting, if able to secure a handy position despite their hold-up tendencies, would benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a late-finishing hold-up type catches a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: Belgarum would need to have set a surprisingly strong pace to create enough attrition for a horse from the back to reel him in; given Balkardy's poor recent form string and Presentandcounting's age, this is an unlikely but possible outcome on good-ground quick ground that can expose stamina limits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Melee Finish
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or early exits disrupt the shape and a tight finish between survivors emerges.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and several horses carrying headgear and uncertain jumping histories, a chaotic finish cannot be completely ruled out; Slaney Opera's consistency and Muskerry Rock's solid recent form make them the steadiest finishers in a muddled scenario.

watchPoints.text: Belgarum's jumping at the later fences — if he has burned energy controlling the pace alone over 3m2f, errors late on could gift the race to a tracking horse, most likely Slaney Opera.

Muskerry Rock's finishing fade flag is critical at this trip — watch whether Harry Skelton commits him early to compensate or allows him to idle, which would leave him with too much to do given his hold-up tendencies.

Balkardy's jumping reliability is a live danger to the field given three non-completions in recent starts — Miss Eleanor Williams on an amateur allowance adds an element of unpredictability in a small field where any incident is magnified.

Presentandcounting's age (12) and weight (168lbs) combined with a hold-up style over 3m2f on Good to Firm ground warrants monitoring — if the pace is strong he may find the trip beyond him late despite a solid sim-going profile.
